newsitem.title: USA: Dutch pig exports slashed by cholera - US attache.
newsitem.headline: Dutch pig exports slashed by cholera - US attache.

text.p: Dutch exports of live pigs are expected to be cut in half this year due to an outbreak of hog cholera, according to a U.S. attache report made public on Monday.

Last year, the Netherlands exported six million live pigs (three million piglets, three million fattening hogs), mostly to other EU member states. As a result of the hog cholera crisis and the EU export ban, Dutch exports of live pigs will be cut in half in 1997, the report prepared by the U.S. embassy in The Hague said.

"The hog cholera crisis theoretically provides an opportunity for the United States to export live pigs to the European Union," the report said. "However, meeting the strict EU import requirements, such as whole herd testing for pseudorabies and hog cholera (a disease the United States does not have), would likely be cost prohibitive."
A total of 65 cases of hog cholera have been confirmed in the Netherlands since the disease outbreak began in February.
Losses of pigs in the Netherlands is expected to increase by two million to 5.5 million head in 1997, the report said. And slaughter numbers are expected to decline by 2.4 million hogs.

The Product Board for Livestock and Meat (PVV) estimates the damage at US$ 530 million, while the Dutch Central Planning Bureau estimates it could range US$ 109 million and US$1.28 billion, the report said.
To contain the spread of the disease, 487,043 pigs have been destroyed to date, the report said. The Dutch government also banned transportation of animals, manure and semen in the infected areas.
"Because new cases continue to occur regularly, there is not a lot of optimism in the Netherlands that the hog cholera crisis will be over soon," the report said.
An EU ban on Dutch pig exports and the Netherlands' own ban on transportation are expected to remain in place for several months, the report said.
Information released in U.S. attache reports is not official U.S. AGriculture Department data.
